claim: Picomolar concentrations of EGFR ligand drive signaling and endocytosis of EGFR in tumors in vivo.
source: Previously we used gene-editing to label endogenous EGF receptor (EGFR) with GFP and demonstrate that picomolar concentrations of EGFR ligand drive signaling and endocytosis of EGFR in tumors in vivo (Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017, which is referenced as the source of this finding.

claim: FAP was inserted in the EGFR extracellular domain using gene-editing.
source: We now use gene-editing to insert a fluorogen activating protein (FAP) in the EGFR extracellular domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the manuscript, including Figure 1A showing the gene-editing strategy and Figure 1B showing Western blot confirmation.

claim: Binding of MG-Bis-SA to FAP-EGFR provides a ratiometric pH-sensitive model with dual fluorescence excitation and a single far-red emission.
source: Binding of the tandem dye pair MG-Bis-SA to FAP-EGFR provides a ratiometric pH-sensitive model with dual fluorescence excitation and a single far-red emission.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, which demonstrates the pH-dependent fluorescence properties of MG-Bis-SA bound to FAP-EGFR.

claim: The excitation ratio of fluorescence intensities faithfully reports the fraction of FAP-EGFR located in acidic endosomal/lysosomal compartments.
source: The excitation ratio of fluorescence intensities was demonstrated to faithfully report the fraction of FAP-EGFR located in acidic endosomal/lysosomal compartments.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 2B showing pH dependence of the 561/640 ratio and Figure 2C showing imaging of FAP-EGFR in endosomes.

claim: A high-throughput assay was developed to measure the rates of clathrin-mediated FAP-EGFR endocytosis stimulated with physiological EGF concentrations.
source: Coupling native FAP-EGFR expression with the high method sensitivity has allowed development of a high-throughput assay to measure the rates of clathrin-mediated FAP-EGFR endocytosis stimulated with physiological EGF concentrations.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4 demonstrating the assay's performance in 96-well plate format.

claim: The assay was utilized to screen a phosphatase siRNA library.
source: The assay was utilized to screen a phosphatase siRNA library.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 4 showing results from screening 240 phosphatases.

claim: Ligand binding to EGFR at the cell surface leads to activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase activity, initiation of multiple signaling cascades and ultimately cell proliferation, differentiation or oncogenic transformation.
source: Ligand binding to EGFR at the cell surface leads to activation of the receptor tyrosine kinase activity, initiation of multiple signaling cascades and ultimately cell proliferation, differentiation or oncogenic transformation (reviewed in Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review by Lemmon and Schlessinger, 2010.

claim: Ligand binding results in rapid endocytosis of EGFR and subsequent degradation of the receptor in lysosomes.
source: Ligand binding also results in rapid endocytosis of EGFR and subsequent degradation of the receptor in lysosomes (reviewed in Sorkin and Goh, 2009a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review by Sorkin and Goh, 2009a.

claim: Endocytosis and lysosomal degradation are thought to be the major regulators of EGFR signaling.
source: Endocytosis and lysosomal degradation are thought to be the major regulators of EGFR signaling (reviewed in Sigismund et al., 2012; Sorkin and von Zastrow, 2009b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to reviews by Sigismund et al., 2012 and Sorkin and von Zastrow, 2009b.

claim: Multiple pathways of EGFR endocytosis have been documented including clathrin-mediated and clathrin-independent endocytosis.
source: Multiple pathways of EGFR endocytosis have been documented including clathrin-mediated (CME) (Gorden et al., 1978; Hanover et al., 1984; Motley et al., 2003) and clathrin-independent endocytosis (for example, Caldieri et al., 2017; Orth et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies documenting different endocytic pathways.

claim: Receptor ubiquitination by the Cbl E3 ubiquitin ligase has been proposed to be one of the redundant mechanisms of the EGFR CME.
source: While receptor ubiquitination by the Cbl E3 ubiquitin ligase has been proposed to be one of the redundant mechanisms of the EGFR CME (Fortian et al., 2015), EGFR internalization was shown to be normal in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from a double-knockout of c-Cbl and Cbl-b (Mohapatra et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fortian et al., 2015 and Mohapatra et al., 2013.

claim: EGFR internalization was shown to be normal in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from a double-knockout of c-Cbl and Cbl-b.
source: While receptor ubiquitination by the Cbl E3 ubiquitin ligase has been proposed to be one of the redundant mechanisms of the EGFR CME (Fortian et al., 2015), EGFR internalization was shown to be normal in mouse embryonic fibroblasts derived from a double-knockout of c-Cbl and Cbl-b (Mohapatra et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mohapatra et al., 2013.

claim: Phosphatases involved in the endocytic process have not been identified despite the well-established importance of the receptor kinase activity and phosphorylation in EGFR CME.
source: Further, despite the well-established importance of the receptor kinase activity and phosphorylation in EGFR CME (reviewed in Sorkin and von Zastrow, 2009b), phosphatases involved in the endocytic process have not been identified.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review by Sorkin and von Zastrow, 2009b and the absence of identified phosphatases.

claim: The use of overexpressed recombinant EGFR and high ligand concentrations favor EGFR internalization through clathrin-independent rather than CME pathways.
source: Specifically, the use of overexpressed recombinant EGFR and high ligand concentrations favor EGFR internalization through clathrin-independent rather than CME pathways.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the discussion of experimental conditions and their effects on endocytic mechanisms.

claim: Low concentrations of EGFR ligands are sufficient to drive EGFR-dependent growth of mouse tumor xenografts.
source: Our recent study using endogenously expressed GFP-tagged EGFR allowed the demonstration that low concentrations of EGFR ligands are sufficient to drive EGFR-dependent growth of mouse tumor xenografts and that EGFR endocytosis in tumors in vivo is clathrin-mediated (Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017.

claim: EGFR endocytosis in tumors in vivo is clathrin-mediated.
source: Our recent study using endogenously expressed GFP-tagged EGFR allowed the demonstration that low concentrations of EGFR ligands are sufficient to drive EGFR-dependent growth of mouse tumor xenografts and that EGFR endocytosis in tumors in vivo is clathrin-mediated (Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017.

claim: MG-Bis-SA is a tandem dye sensor consisting of a fluorogenic acceptor, MG, and a pH-dependent Cy3 FRET donor.
source: To develop and employ a quantitative internalization assay, EE7 cells were labeled with MG-Bis-SA, a tandem dye sensor consisting of a fluorogenic acceptor, MG, and a pH-dependent Cy3 FRET (fluorescence resonance energy transfer) donor (Perkins et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Perkins et al., 2018b.

claim: At low pH, Cy3 absorption and energy transfer to MG are increased.
source: At low pH, Cy3 (donor) absorption and energy transfer to MG are increased.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the dye system described in the manuscript and cited literature.

claim: MG fluorescence (680–700 nm) by direct excitation at 640 nm is independent of pH.
source: Therefore, the excitation contribution of the pH-sensitive moiety (561 nm excitation) to far-red emission (680–700 nm) from the MG-FAP complex, increases at an acidic pH, whereas MG fluorescence (680–700 nm) by direct excitation at 640 nm is independent of pH.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the dye system described in the manuscript.

claim: The 561/640 ratio of MG-Bis-SA bound to FAP-EGFR was ~3 fold higher at pH 5.5 than at pH 7.4.
source: In our measurements in EE7 cells, the 561/640 ratio of MG-Bis-SA bound to FAP-EGFR was ~3 fold higher at pH 5.5 than at pH 7.4 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: FAP was inserted at the amino-terminus of the EGFR molecule in the EGFR gene locus downstream of the sequence encoding the signal peptide and upstream of the sequence of the mature EGFR using CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing method.
source: To generate the pH-sensitive EGFR, FAP was inserted at the amino-terminus of the EGFR molecule in the EGFR gene locus downstream of the sequence encoding the signal peptide and upstream of the sequence of the mature EGFR using CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing method (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and Figure 1A showing the gene-editing strategy.

claim: Genome editing was performed in HeLa cells because EGFR endocytosis and signaling have been extensively studied and well characterized in these cells.
source: Genome editing was performed in HeLa cells because EGFR endocytosis and signaling have been extensively studied and well characterized in these cells by others and ourselves.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about HeLa cells as a model system.

claim: FAP was inserted in all three copies of the EGFR gene in the EE7 clone as no untagged EGFR was detected.
source: Western blotting analysis confirmed FAP-EGFR fusion and demonstrated that FAP was inserted in all three copies of the EGFR gene in the EE7 clone as no untagged EGFR was detected (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The EE7 clone expressed a higher level of EGFR compared to parental HeLa cells.
source: While this clone did express a higher level of EGFR compared to parental HeLa cells, the activity of FAP-EGFR in EE7 cells measured as receptor phosphorylation at Tyr1068 per ligand-occupied receptor was equivalent to parental HeLa cells (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: The activity of FAP-EGFR in EE7 cells measured as receptor phosphorylation at Tyr1068 per ligand-occupied receptor was equivalent to parental HeLa cells.
source: While this clone did express a higher level of EGFR compared to parental HeLa cells, the activity of FAP-EGFR in EE7 cells measured as receptor phosphorylation at Tyr1068 per ligand-occupied receptor was equivalent to parental HeLa cells (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: The 125I-EGF internalization rates were high and essentially similar in parental HeLa and EE7 cells (Ke = 0.49–0.51/min).
source: The 125I-EGF internalization rates were high and also essentially similar in parental HeLa and EE7 cells (Ke = 0.49–0.51/min; Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Internalization rates of 0.49-0.51/min are within the range of typical internalization rates via clathrin-coated pits.
source: Such rates are within the range of typical internalization rates via clathrin-coated pits (reviewed in Sorkin and Goh, 2009a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review by Sorkin and Goh, 2009a.

claim: The insertion of a large tag, such as YFP, in the amino-terminus of EGFR does not affect receptor activity and endocytosis.
source: The functionality of FAP-EGFR demonstrated in Figure 1B–E is consistent with the previous demonstration that the insertion of a large tag, such as YFP, in the amino-terminus of EGFR does not affect receptor activity and endocytosis (Kozer et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kozer et al., 2011.

claim: MG-B-Tau accumulated strongly in endosomes where it co-localized with EGF-Rh after 15 min EGF stimulation.
source: Figure 1F shows strong accumulation of MG-B-Tau in endosomes where it is appropriately co-localized with EGF-Rh.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The value of the 561/640 ratio increased during the first 10–15 min after EGF stimulation at 37°C reaching a plateau at 15 min.
source: The value of the 561/640 ratio increased during the first 10–15 min after EGF (1–20 ng/ml) stimulation at 37°C reaching a plateau at 15 min (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Z'-factor was calculated to be 0.76–0.88, indicating the high robustness of the assay.
source: To test the robustness of the assay at physiologically relevant EGF concentrations, we calculated the Z'-factor from the assay run with half a plate run as control and the other half with the addition of 1, 2 or 4 ng/ml EGF. The Z'-factor was calculated to be 0.76–0.88, indicating the high robustness of the assay.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Concentrations of EGFR ligands accessible to EGFR in mammalian tissues are typically below 1–2 ng/ml.
source: Concentrations of EGFR ligands accessible to EGFR in mammalian tissues are typically below 1–2 ng/ml (Connolly and Rose, 1988; Dvorak, 2010; Hirata and Orth, 1979; Ishikawa et al., 2005; Murdoch-Kinch et al., 2011; Oka and Orth, 1983; Rich et al., 2017), and our recent studies suggested that concentration of EGFR ligands of 1 ng/ml or less are present in mouse tumor xenografts and are sufficient to support EGFR-dependent tumor growth (Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies measuring EGFR ligand concentrations in tissues.

claim: Concentration of EGFR ligands of 1 ng/ml or less are present in mouse tumor xenografts and are sufficient to support EGFR-dependent tumor growth.
source: Concentrations of EGFR ligands accessible to EGFR in mammalian tissues are typically below 1–2 ng/ml (Connolly and Rose, 1988; Dvorak, 2010; Hirata and Orth, 1979; Ishikawa et al., 2005; Murdoch-Kinch et al., 2011; Oka and Orth, 1983; Rich et al., 2017), and our recent studies suggested that concentration of EGFR ligands of 1 ng/ml or less are present in mouse tumor xenografts and are sufficient to support EGFR-dependent tumor growth (Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pinilla-Macua et al., 2017.

claim: Endocytosis of FAP-EGFR stimulated with low EGF concentrations was blocked by the inhibitor of EGFR kinase activity (PD158780).
source: Importantly, endocytosis of FAP-EGFR stimulated with low EGF concentrations was blocked by the inhibitor of EGFR kinase activity (PD158780), whereas a significant component of kinase-insensitive FAP-EGFR endocytosis was observed when high, saturating concentrations of EGF were used (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A significant component of kinase-insensitive FAP-EGFR endocytosis was observed when high, saturating concentrations of EGF were used.
source: Importantly, endocytosis of FAP-EGFR stimulated with low EGF concentrations was blocked by the inhibitor of EGFR kinase activity (PD158780), whereas a significant component of kinase-insensitive FAP-EGFR endocytosis was observed when high, saturating concentrations of EGF were used (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: EGFR tyrosine kinase activity is important at low concentrations of EGF (conditions favoring internalization through the CME pathway) but not at high EGF concentrations (conditions favoring clathrin-independent endocytosis).
source: These data are consistent with the concept that EGFR tyrosine kinase activity is important at low concentrations of EGF (conditions favoring internalization through the CME pathway) but not at high EGF concentrations (conditions favoring clathrin-independent endocytosis) (Chen et al., 1989; Honegger et al., 1987; Lund et al., 1990; Sorkina et al., 2002; Wiley, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to studies examining the role of kinase activity in EGFR endocytosis.

claim: FAP-EGFR endocytosis was strongly inhibited by CHC and dynamin-2 depletion.
source: As shown in the dual-flashlight plot that represents a summary of three independent repeats of screening experiments (Figure 4C), FAP-EGFR endocytosis was strongly inhibited by CHC and dynamin-2 depletion, confirming that under conditions of this assay the endocytosis is clathrin-mediated.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C from the siRNA screening.

claim: Under conditions of this assay the endocytosis is clathrin-mediated.
source: As shown in the dual-flashlight plot that represents a summary of three independent repeats of screening experiments (Figure 4C), FAP-EGFR endocytosis was strongly inhibited by CHC and dynamin-2 depletion, confirming that under conditions of this assay the endocytosis is clathrin-mediated.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing inhibition by CHC and dynamin-2 depletion in Figure 4C.

claim: Several siRNA pools to phosphatases were found to significantly inhibit FAP-EGFR endocytosis.
source: Several siRNA pools to phosphatases were found to significantly inhibit FAP-EGFR endocytosis (Figure 4C and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and source data.

claim: IPDD5D (SHIP1), INDDL1 (SHIP2) and INDD4A are phosphotidyl-inositide phosphatases identified in the screen as potentially important for EGFR endocytosis.
source: Interestingly, among phosphatases identified in the screen as potentially important for EGFR endocytosis, are several phosphotidyl-inositide phosphatases, such as IPDD5D (SHIP1) (Figure 4C), INDDL1 (SHIP2) (Figure 4—source data 1) and INDD4A (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the siRNA screen shown in Figure 4C and source data.

claim: SHIP1, SHIP2 and INDD4A have been implicated in various endocytic processes.
source: All three phosphatases have been implicated in various endocytic processes (Erneux et al., 2011; Kamen et al., 2007; Nigorikawa et al., 2015), and SHIP2 has been previously shown to be important for CME (Nakatsu et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on these phosphatases.

claim: SHIP2 has been previously shown to be important for CME.
source: All three phosphatases have been implicated in various endocytic processes (Erneux et al., 2011; Kamen et al., 2007; Nigorikawa et al., 2015), and SHIP2 has been previously shown to be important for CME (Nakatsu et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nakatsu et al., 2010.

claim: PTPRH has been implicated in dephosphorylation of EGFR.
source: Several other phosphatases identified in our screens as potential regulators of EGFR endocytosis, such as PTPRH (Figure 4C), have been implicated in dephosphorylation of EGFR (Yao et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yao et al., 2017.

claim: EGFR endocytosis has been previously analyzed using high-throughput screens of targeted and whole-genome siRNA libraries.
source: EGFR endocytosis has been previously analyzed using high-throughput screens of targeted and whole-genome siRNA libraries (Collinet et al., 2010; Pelkmans et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Collinet et al., 2010 and Pelkmans et al., 2005.

claim: Previous high-throughput screens used labeled EGF to follow endocytosis of EGFR and a complex multi-parameter single-cell image analysis to score for the effects of siRNAs.
source: These studies used labeled EGF to follow endocytosis of EGFR and a complexed multi-parameter single-cell image analysis to score for the effects of siRNAs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the cited studies and their methodologies.

claim: Previous screens required high concentrations of labeled EGF.
source: Importantly, the downstream analysis in those screens required high concentrations of labeled EGF.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the cited studies and their methodologies.

claim: The FAP-based method allows exquisitely sensitive screening for regulators of the constitutive EGFR endocytosis.
source: Therefore, the FAP-based method allows exquisitely sensitive screening for regulators of the constitutive EGFR endocytosis, and EGFR endocytosis induced by other EGFR ligands, that are technically difficult to label.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the demonstrated capabilities of the method.

claim: The FAP-based method can be used to study ligand-independent endocytosis, such as endocytosis induced by activated p38 MAP kinase.
source: Also, as we are directly and selectively labeling surface EGFR, it can be used to study ligand-independent endocytosis, such as endocytosis induced by activated p38 MAP kinase (Frey et al., 2006; Vergarajauregui et al., 2006; Zwang and Yarden, 2006).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the method's capabilities and citations to studies on p38 MAP kinase-induced endocytosis.

claim: Constitutive endocytosis of EGFR has been previously studied by measuring the uptake rates of radiolabeled and biotinylated antibodies bound to the EGFR extracellular domain.
source: Constitutive endocytosis of EGFR has been previously studied by measuring the uptake rates of radiolabeled and biotinylated antibodies bound to the EGFR extracellular domain (Burke et al., 2001; Burke and Wiley, 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Burke et al., 2001 and Burke and Wiley, 1999.

claim: Antibody-based measurements can be affected by the inability of an antibody to recognize receptors irrespective of their conformation and ligand occupancy, and by the bi-valent IgG binding.
source: Further, antibody-based measurements can be affected by the inability of an antibody to recognize receptors irrespective of their conformation and ligand occupancy, and by the bi-valent IgG binding; and these assays involve a 'terminal' antibody-stripping step at 4°C at each point of a time-course.
evidence: The claim is based on known limitations of antibody-based methods.

claim: FAP-EGFR live-cell imaging can be performed on a pixel-by-pixel basis at high resolution, and thus can report the subcellular localization of the receptor in living cells.
source: Second, FAP-EGFR live-cell imaging can be performed on a pixel-by-pixel basis at high resolution, and thus can report the subcellular localization of the receptor in living cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the demonstrated capabilities of the imaging method.

claim: The fold-increase of the endolysosomal 561-nm-excited fluorescence of MG-Bis-SA bound to FAP-EGFR during endocytosis is significantly higher than the fold-increase of the total cellular fluorescence at 561 nm excitation.
source: The fold-increase of the endolysosomal 561-nm-excited fluorescence of MG-Bis-SA bound to FAP-EGFR during endocytosis of this complex is significantly higher that the fold-increase of the total cellular fluorescence at 561 nm excitation (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Various types of cells may display different kinetics and mechanisms of constitutive and stimuli-induced endocytosis.
source: Because various types of cells may display different kinetics and mechanisms of constitutive and stimuli-induced endocytosis (see for example Burke and Wiley, 1999; Jiang et al., 2003; Mohapatra et al., 2013), application of the MG-Bis-SA/FAP-EGFR approach would require a FAP knock-in in each cell line of interest.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies showing cell-type differences in endocytosis.

claim: Engineering the FAP-EGFR by CRISPR/Cas9 method in human cell lines will be dramatically facilitated by the availability of the donor construct, efficient gRNAs and other technical information obtained in experiments with HeLa cells.
source: However, engineering the FAP-EGFR by CRISPR/Cas9 method in human cell lines will be dramatically facilitated by the availability of the donor construct, efficient gRNAs and other technical information obtained in our experiments with HeLa cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference about the utility of the developed tools for future applications.

claim: It is feasible to generate a cell line expressing endogenous FAP-EGFR within 1 month using the developed tools.
source: We believe that using these tools it is feasible to generate a cell line expressing endogenous FAP-EGFR within 1 month.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the authors' experience and the tools developed.

claim: Tagging transmembrane proteins with pH-sensitive fluorescent proteins, such as pHluorin, has been widely used for studying membrane trafficking.
source: Tagging transmembrane proteins ('cargo') with pH-sensitive fluorescent proteins (FPs), such as pHluorin, has been widely used (reviewed in Bizzarri et al., 2009), but this approach has a major disadvantage due to its inability to distinguish biosynthetic and internalized pools of intracellular FP-tagged cargo.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review by Bizzarri et al., 2009.

claim: The pHluorin approach has a major disadvantage due to its inability to distinguish biosynthetic and internalized pools of intracellular FP-tagged cargo.
source: Tagging transmembrane proteins ('cargo') with pH-sensitive fluorescent proteins (FPs), such as pHluorin, has been widely used (reviewed in Bizzarri et al., 2009), but this approach has a major disadvantage due to its inability to distinguish biosynthetic and internalized pools of intracellular FP-tagged cargo.
evidence: The claim is based on known limitations of pHluorin-based methods.

claim: Methods using pH-sensitive fluorophores conjugated to genetically encoded tags, such as SNAP or Halo, often require long incubations with the fluorophore dye, washing off unbound fluorophores and may result in substantial background fluorescence.
source: A number of methods using pH-sensitive fluorophores that can be conjugated to genetically encoded tags, such as SNAP or Halo, were also applied to study membrane traffic (Los and Wood, 2007; Martineau et al., 2017; Takeda et al., 2012). However, such methods often require long incubations with the fluorophore dye, washing off unbound fluorophores and may result in substantial background fluorescence.
evidence: The claim is based on known limitations of SNAP/Halo-based methods cited in the manuscript.

claim: SRpHi are excellent endosomal pH probes but they are not intended for labeling of endocytic cargo.
source: Recently developed radiometric pH biosensors called SRpHi are excellent endosomal pH probes but they are not intended for labeling of endocytic cargo (Richardson et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Richardson et al., 2017.

claim: In the FAP-based approach, low backgrounds are achieved due to the 'dark' state of unbound MG.
source: In the FAP-based approach, low backgrounds are achieved due to the 'dark' state of unbound MG.
evidence: The claim is based on the known properties of the MG fluorogen.

claim: Labeling of surface-exposed FP-tagged cargo with MG-Bis-SA is virtually instantaneous.
source: Moreover, labeling of surface-exposed FP-tagged cargo with MG-Bis-SA is virtually instantaneous, which allows monitoring the endocytic process from its initial steps at the plasma membrane and through the sorting in endosomes without an interference from constitutive endosomal and biosynthetic pools of the cargo.
evidence: The claim is based on the demonstrated properties of MG-Bis-SA binding to FAP.

claim: MG-Bis-SA labeling allows monitoring the endocytic process from its initial steps at the plasma membrane and through the sorting in endosomes without an interference from constitutive endosomal and biosynthetic pools of the cargo.
source: Moreover, labeling of surface-exposed FP-tagged cargo with MG-Bis-SA is virtually instantaneous, which allows monitoring the endocytic process from its initial steps at the plasma membrane and through the sorting in endosomes without an interference from constitutive endosomal and biosynthetic pools of the cargo.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the properties of the method and demonstrated data.

claim: The effectiveness of MG-Bis-SA for studying endocytosis and recycling of FAP-tagged β2-adrenergic receptor overexpressed in HEK293 cells at single-endosome level was demonstrated.
source: In the latter study, the effectiveness of MG-Bis-SA for studying endocytosis and recycling of FAP-tagged β2-adrenergic receptor (B2AR) overexpressed in HEK293 cells at single-endosome level was demonstrated.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Perkins et al., 2018b.

claim: FAP-tagged antibodies and nanobodies to EGFR have been previously developed to study EGFR expression and endocytosis in cells with high receptor levels.
source: We have previously developed FAP-tagged antibodies and nanobodies to EGFR to study its expression and endocytosis in cells with high receptor levels (Ackerman et al., 2018; Tan et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies by the authors.

claim: An assay with a Z'-factor between 0.5 and 1 is considered excellent for HTS.
source: An assay with a Z`-factor between 0.5 and 1 is considered excellent for HTS (Zhang et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 1999.
